read.text:
How to read these

Grey boxes are content; blue marks the ONE main action on each screen, which is always the job's next step.

Press Play on any artboard with a blue mark: links between screens work (Today → Open → Job → Clear blockers → Packet, and so on).

Data is the demo company (Hartline Remodeling). Every screen has its own address, shown under the tabs.

jobnote.text:
Rules these screens follow

1. One primary button per screen: Clear blockers → Approve & send → Send waiver → Match payment → Draft pay app → Close.
2. Everything else is a secondary row; explanations live in tooltips and (i) help.
3. Status is a word in a pill (Blocked, Ready to send, Sent, Paid); the full sentence sits under it.
4. Dates read like Aug 12, 2026.
5. Before any send, the screen lists recipient, copy, amount and attachments.

queue.text:
Today's list, most urgent first

1. Job's done? (a text or email): Mark done and draft
2. Ready to send: Review & send (opens the job)
3. Waiver due: Review waiver (opens the job)
4. Due soon: the payer's pay-app cutoff is within 5 days and nothing is billed this cycle: Bill progress
5. Blocked: Clear N blockers (opens the packet)
6. Follow up, past the payer's window: Send follow-up, one tap; the row names the recipient
7. Finished work not billed: Draft pay app, one tap (sends nothing)
8. Inbox item with a suggested job: File to this job, one tap

One next step per job; a cutoff within 5 days is added to that job's row and moves it up.

money.text:
Money is one destination with tabs: Pay apps, Packets, Change orders, Collections, Payments, Waivers, Retainage, Outbox.

Settings holds Team & account (your name, the company's details for every pay app, the team, Billing and two-step sign-in), Payer playbook (with each payer's monthly pay-app cutoff), Audit (with the hash-chain check), Help, and Helper answers for the founders.

phone.text:
Phone layout

Top bar with a menu button; the five destinations open in a drawer.
Tabs scroll sideways.
Every table becomes one card per row, each value labelled.
The main action is full width; on Today the buttons sit under each row's text.
Every control is at least 44 px tall.
The job record has "take a photo", which opens the camera.

newrow.text:
What these add

Results: counted from the company's own pay apps and payments; nothing estimated. A monthly summary email goes to the owner.

Payments: QuickBooks payments are proposed, never recorded until ticked, from a CSV export or, once connected, from QuickBooks itself (read-only); each is recorded once. "Check against QuickBooks" lists the differences.

Playbook: a rejection or pencil-copy change becomes a suggested packet item; nothing changes until Add to packet. The pay-app cutoff is a contract date, not a legal one.

History, Outbox and Audit load 50 rows at a time.

outside.text:
Outside the app

The payer page is linked from each pay app email. It shows the lines, the packet documents and the PDF, and Mark as received updates the job.

The signing page is emailed for a pending change order. The typed name, consent, time, network address and a fingerprint of what was shown are kept. Counsel should check the consent wording.
